cues.zh: 让你做到以前做不到的事。我们其实不太关心某个特定工具有什么问题。就说 TypeScript 吧，它2016年出现。五年时间里，它从一种还算常用的东西，变成了……我的意思是，现在写的代码很大一部分都是 TypeScript。

cues.zh: TypeScript 很酷，因为你写的还是 JavaScript。TypeScript 允许你写地道的 JavaScript。它让你能用更地道的方式标注类型。你还能获得那种从 Java 和 C# 里习惯了的类型安全。某种程度上，TypeScript 甚至更精巧，因为 JavaScript 不是 C# 也不是 Java。有些模式需要类型标注，而用没有针对它定制的类型系统很难处理。所以 TypeScript 挺好的。

cues.en: And by that, I mean, you know, back in the early days of computing, you would learn how to write software, meaning you would learn how to write a program with pencil and paper, you would carefully craft it, you know, then you would go meticulously punch it and it had to be perfect. You would run it through the punch code verifier, which would check your program for syntactical errors. Then you would submit it to the computer operator who would put you in a queue. And maybe in 12 hours, your program would run, it would run for an hour, and then it would crash.
cues.zh: 我这么说，是因为你知道，在计算机发展的早期，学写软件，也就是学着用纸笔写程序。你得仔细构思，再一丝不苟地把程序打成穿孔卡片，而且必须完全正确。之后还要把卡片送进穿孔代码验证器，检查程序有没有语法错误。然后你把程序交给计算机操作员，他会把你排进队列。可能要等上 12 个小时，程序才能运行。它运行一个小时，然后就崩溃了。

cues.en: That was software development, right? So everything about software development was happening in the static domain of the program and not in the dynamic domain, running the program. So developing programs was not an interactive process. 12 hours is not an interactive process, right? And yes, computers have become faster and we've collapsed this interaction.
cues.zh: 这就是以前的软件开发，对吧？软件开发的一切都发生在程序的静态领域，而不是在运行程序的动态领域。所以开发程序并不是一个交互式的过程。耗时 12 个小时可算不上交互式过程，对吧？当然，计算机越来越快，我们大幅缩短了这种交互周期。

cues.en: But at the same time, when I watch how people use modern tools, it is a batch-oriented programming model. You write some code, you fix your type errors, you write some tests, and then you run your program and it doesn't work. And you just start over. It is a batch-oriented process. And no mainstream programming language that's popular is really doing much about it. There's almost everything you will see as a mitigation.
cues.zh: 但与此同时，当我观察大家如何使用现代工具时，发现它仍然是一种批处理式的编程模式。你写点代码，修复类型错误，写几个测试，然后运行程序，结果跑不通。于是你只能从头再来。这就是一个批处理式的过程。而且当下流行的主流编程语言几乎都没怎么着手解决这个问题。你看到的大多数手段，充其量只算得上是权宜之计。

cues.en: usually via an IDE. Like you can run this test, this one test, you can do this, but it's not a very interactive model. And so this is not a new idea. These problems, the problem with sort of a batch oriented approach to software development was solved 40, 50 years ago. You know, I think I've given a bunch of talks. I think I've talked about this book many times. I'm happy to see that StripePress put it out in hardcover. It's the dream machine.
cues.zh: 通常是通过 IDE 来运行。你可以运行这个测试、单独运行某一个测试，也可以做这些事，但这种模式的交互性不强。这并不是什么新想法。软件开发中这种偏批处理的方式所带来的问题，早在四五十年前就解决了。你知道，我做过不少演讲，也多次提到这本书。很高兴看到 Stripe Press 出了精装版，书名是《梦想机器》。

If you haven't read it, you should run out and read it. If you're a software developer, this is essential reading. And I think what's fascinating is that you get to a certain point and you realize what real improvements have been made. This book actually stops right before the arrival of
cues.zh: 我是通过阅读Smalltalk邮件列表熟悉这段历史的。还有Alan Kay的这本书，这是关于交互式计算最好的历史著作之一。我拿起这本书就爱上了它。如果你还没读过，应该赶紧去读。如果你是软件开发人员，这是必读之作。我觉得最吸引人的是，读到某个节点你会意识到真正的改进是什么。这本书实际上正好停在

cues.en: you know, widespread personal computing. It's setting the stage for that story, but it shows all of the innovations and research that went into making computers more interactive, because everybody knew that batch-oriented programming was not the way it should be done. Really, not everybody. Almost no one. A few visionaries convinced the rest of the world that it could be better. One of these, and just to drive this point home before I talk about John McCarthy, who was talked about in this book,
cues.zh: 你知道，个人计算普及之前。它在为那个故事搭台，但展示了所有让计算机更具交互性的创新和研究，因为大家都知道批处理式编程不是正确的做法。其实，也不是所有人。几乎没人这么想。是少数有远见的人说服了世界其他地方，事情可以做得更好。其中一位，而且为了在讲John McCarthy之前把这一点说透——书里也提到了他——

cues.en: You know, what do I mean, right? So it doesn't matter what programming language you use, whether that's TypeScript or Java or C or C++ or JavaScript or Python or Ruby, who cares, Erlang, it doesn't matter. The one thing that every modern developer knows and loves is the shell. The shell is a kind of interactive development process that lets you get into the dynamic behavior of your system.
cues.zh: 你知道我什么意思吧？不管你用什么编程语言，TypeScript、Java、C、C++、JavaScript、Python、Ruby，谁在乎呢，Erlang，都无所谓。每个现代开发者都熟悉并喜爱的一样东西就是shell。shell是一种交互式开发过程，让你能深入系统的动态行为。

cues.en: So imagine for a second a shell, a command line interface that didn't let you change directories. Imagine a command line interface that didn't let you examine the contents of files. Imagine a command line interface that didn't let you install and update programs. This is not a tool we would use, right? So much of what we do is defined by our ability to interact with the system via the shell. Yet when you look at
cues.zh: 想象一下，一个不让你切换目录的shell，一个命令行界面。想象一个不让你查看文件内容的命令行界面。想象一个不让你安装和更新程序的命令行界面。这种工具我们根本不会用，对吧？我们所做的很多事情，都取决于我们能否通过shell与系统交互。然而当你看看

cues.en: the current crop of mainstream programming languages, they say that they have this thing called a REPL, but this REPL would not even satisfy the most basic requirements for the CLI. You know, imagine a REPL that didn't let you change between modules, right? A module is like a directory. Almost every modern programming language is the concept of a module. You can't switch into a module.
cues.zh: 在当下主流的编程语言里，他们说有一种叫 REPL 的东西，但这个 REPL 连命令行界面的基本要求都达不到。想象一下，一个 REPL 连切换模块都不行，对吧？模块就像一个目录。几乎所有现代编程语言都有模块这个概念，但你却不能切换到某个模块里。

cues.en: A REPL generally puts you into a global module, and you can import things, but you can't get inside a module and poke around and see what's going on and what is the relationship from the perspective things within that module. Many REPLs don't let you do this. You can't reflect on that module. You can't REPL into it, and then you can't see it. And then finally, a very few REPLs let you install and update functions inside those modules, right? Again,
cues.zh: REPL 通常会把你带到一个全局模块里，你可以导入东西，但你没法进入某个模块，四处看看里面发生了什么，也看不到从模块内部视角出发，各个东西之间是什么关系。很多 REPL 都不支持这样做。你没法反射这个模块，也没法进入它的 REPL，更看不到它的内容。最后，只有极少数 REPL 允许你在这些模块里安装和更新函数，对吧？再说一次，

cues.en: Nobody would use a CLI that worked this way, yet this is the interactive interface that even advanced programming languages ship that are in popular use. And this to me is very strange because if you think about it, your program is a computer system. It is something that you would like to shell into and you would like to have the same power that you have at the shell.
cues.zh: 没人会去用这么难用的命令行工具，但很多当前流行的高级编程语言，自带的交互界面偏偏就是这副模样。对我来说这太奇怪了，因为仔细想想，你的程序本身就是一个计算机系统，你会希望能直接登录进去，拥有像在 shell 里一样的操控能力。

cues.en: But again, it is not a common feature. And this innovation came from John McCarthy. John McCarthy is most famous for pointing the term artificial intelligence. And he saw what people were doing with this sort of batch, hard-based programming. He said, no way. I'm not interested. I'm calculating cool. You could do calculation that way. But that's not what I'm interested in. I want to do mathematics. I want to do logic. I want to be able to
cues.zh: 但话说回来，这并不是个常见的功能。而这项创新其实源于 John McCarthy，他最出名的事迹是提出了“人工智能”这个词。当时他看到人们在搞这种基于打孔卡片的批处理编程，便说：绝不可能，我毫无兴趣；拿来做数值计算确实不错，你们爱怎么算怎么算，但这不是我想搞的，我想做的是数学，是逻辑，我想能够

cues.en: input abstract things into the computer. As I can transform them with pencil and paper, the computer should be able to do that. I don't want to have to submit and wait 12 hours. On a pencil and paper, I can type in an equation and do the transformations instantly. So there are two things he created. One was the concept of time sharing so that multiple programmers could share time on a computer. And the other thing is he invented the REPL.
cues.zh: 把抽象的东西输入到电脑里。既然我能用纸笔变换它们，电脑也应该能做到。我不想提交后就等上12个小时。用纸笔，我可以输入一个方程，立刻完成变换。所以他创造了两样东西。一是分时概念，让多个程序员可以共享电脑的时间。另一样是他发明了REPL。

cues.en: so that he could write a mathematical expression in LISP syntax, and he could have definitions for the transformations, or he could have a theorem prover built in, and it would transform a proof entered in LISP syntax, and he would get the result in real time. By time sharing and adding this interactive loop, he was able to have higher level thoughts.
cues.zh: 这样他就能用 LISP 语法写出数学表达式，还能为变换提供定义，或者内置一个定理证明器，它能转换用 LISP 语法输入的证明，他就能实时得到结果。通过分时和加入这个交互循环，他得以进行更高层次的思考。

cues.en: people were obsessed with this particular mode of problems that computers could solve. And he saw the ability to solve things that people had not even conceived could be done with computers. And perhaps allow us to do things we had never imagined with pencil and paper. So, you know, Lisp is 57. And then you have people like Alan Kay, who completely subsumed those ideas that we can go way further. We can go way further.
cues.zh: 人们痴迷于计算机能解决的这类特定问题。而他看到了解决那些人们甚至从未想过计算机能做的事的能力。也许还能让我们做到用纸笔从未想象过的事。所以，你知道，Lisp 已经 57 岁了。然后还有像 Alan Kay 这样的人，他完全吸收了这些想法，认为我们可以走得更远。我们可以走得更远。

cues.en: This is an image of Smalltalk. And going back to my shell analogy, in Smalltalk, you had a system browser. The system browser was laid out like a file system. In the top left, you have all the different types of categories and classes. The first one is collections that are sequential. In that category, you have interval, linked list, map collection, order collection, sort of collection. You could drill down just like you do with a file browser.
cues.zh: 这是一张 Smalltalk 的界面截图。回到我之前提到的 shell 类比，在 Smalltalk 里有一个系统浏览器。它的布局像文件系统。左上角列出了各种类别和类。第一个类别是顺序集合。里面有区间、链表、映射集合、有序集合、排序集合。你可以像使用文件浏览器那样逐层浏览。

cues.en: You can see the categories of the types of methods. And then you can select the method that you're interested in. And you can see that source code. But more importantly, you can edit the contents of the method submitted to the system and the whole system updates. And that collection now has updated behavior. So this is a programming environment that has at least the amount of power one does from a command line interface. Something that people do not currently have because
cues.zh: 你可以看到方法类型的分类，然后选择你感兴趣的方法，查看它的源代码。更重要的是，你可以编辑提交到系统中的方法内容，整个系统也会随之更新。这组内容现在的行为也更新了。所以，这种编程环境至少有命令行界面那样强大的功能。现在人们还没有这样的环境，因为

cues.en: mainstream programming languages, they front load into the static part, the sort of batch programming part, but they really offer almost no affordances for the dynamic part of the development cycle. What's going to happen when I run my program, right?
